guides: Hi, I'm Echo. I show you around on the real screens, half a minute a lesson. Stop me any time.
Four ways in. A file, your voice, a meeting or a link. Each card opens its own window.
Four ways in. The plus button opens all four: a file, your voice, a meeting or a link.
Start with a file. MP3, MP4, WAV, any recording. Press this card and the upload opens. Next opens it for you.
Start with a file. MP3, MP4, WAV, any recording. Press the plus, then Audio and video files. Next opens it for you.
The file goes here. Drop a recording here, or press Upload file and pick one. I wait: the next steps show up once the file is in.
The file goes here. Press Upload file and pick a recording. I wait: the next steps show up once the file is in.
Transcription language. The language spoken in the recording. English is set; change it when the call was in another language.
Speaker identification. Switch it on when more than one person spoke, and keep Auto-detect: it counts the voices itself. Set a number only when you are sure.
Template and folder. Both optional. A template shapes the summary, a folder is where the recording lands. Both can be set later.
Press Start transcription. That is all. The transcript is ready in minutes, and this lesson is done the moment the upload starts.
Open the welcome recording. Every transcript is a row here. I made this one for you. Next opens it.
A recording. The transcript on the left, the tools above it, notes and outline on the right.
The title is yours. Click it to rename. Underneath: who made it, the folder, the speakers, the source and the length.
The title is yours. Tap it to rename. Underneath: who made it, the folder, the speakers, the source and the length.
Transcript and Summary. Transcript is every word, as it was said. Summary is the notes. We start on the transcript.
Click a timecode. The player jumps to that moment. While it plays, the words follow the voice.
Play, back, forward. Play starts where you are. The arrows step back or forward five seconds when you missed a word.
Set the pace. Half speed for a fast talker, double speed for a long call.
Hide the names. I switched Speakers off: the text reads as one clean block. Switch it back any time.
And the timecodes. Timestamps go the same way. I put both back for you.
Back to the welcome recording. Same file as before. Next opens it.
Translate to. The transcript and the summary, in another language. Next opens the list.
Pick a language. Dozens of them. I'll take Spanish for this one.
Then press Translate. Spanish is picked. The Translate button next to it starts the work.
It starts at once. On a phone there is nothing more to press: the work starts the moment you pick a language.
A tab for each language. The Spanish transcript opens next to the original. Nothing is replaced: switch between them any time.
Copy or export it. Copy and Export now ask which language you want.
Edit transcript. A name, a term, a word the model misheard. Next turns the text into editing.
Click straight into the text. Every block is a field now. I put the cursor in the first one: type to fix it, like in any document.
Undo, reset, save. Undo steps back one change. Reset to original brings back what the model wrote. Save keeps it for everyone you share with.
Nothing is lost. Timecodes and speakers stay where they are. I leave editing now without saving.
Three voices, three names. The app heard three people and took their names from the call. Next opens the list.
Rename, add, remove. Click a name to rename it. Remove a voice and its blocks go to someone else.
Rename, add, remove. Tap a name to rename it. Remove a voice and its blocks go to someone else.
Wrong name on one block. Click the name on that block and pick who really said it.
Wrong name on one block. Tap the name on that block and pick who really said it.
Two people in one block. Select the other person's words and pick their name. Only those words move.
The Summary tab. Notes written from the transcript: the decisions, the action items, what to remember.
Apply template. A template decides the shape: meeting notes, interview, lecture, action items. Pick one and the summary is rewritten in it.
All templates live here. Next takes you to the Templates page.
Templates. Every way a summary can be written, built in and yours.
Ready to use. Meeting notes, interviews, lectures and more. Star the ones you use and they stay close.
See it before you apply. Open a template to read its example summary. Then apply it from any recording.
Export. Everything about this recording, as files. Next opens the options.
Transcript. PDF, Word, plain text or subtitles. Choose whether speaker names and timestamps go in.
Summary, translation, audio. Each one is a switch. Turn on what you need, the rest stays out.
One click. Several files come as one zip. I close this for you now.
Share. Invite people by email or turn on a link. Next opens it.
Who can see it. Only the people you invite, or anyone with the link. They see the recording, its transcript and its summary.
Or just copy. No invite needed when you only want the words. Next opens Copy.
Or just copy. No invite needed when you only want the words. Copy is under More; Next opens it.
Transcript or summary. Either one goes straight to your clipboard, ready to paste into an email or a doc.
Shared with me. Recordings other people share with you land here.
Where recordings live. My Records, in the sidebar. Next takes you there.
My Records. Every recording you own, in one table. Tabs above, folders in the sidebar.
Recent, Starred, Shared, Trash. Star what you come back to. Trash keeps deleted recordings until you empty it.
Create a folder. One per client or project. Next opens the form.
A name and a colour. That is all a folder needs. It appears in the sidebar the moment you press Create.
Move recordings. Tick one or more and choose Move to folder. You can also pick a folder while uploading.
Share a whole folder. Hover a folder and press the people icon. Everyone invited sees every recording in it.
Where your calls live. Meetings, in the sidebar. Next takes you there.
Meetings. Your calendar with a recorder attached. Upcoming, past, and the calendars you connected.
Connect your calendar. Press Connect next to Google Calendar. The rest of this lesson needs your meetings, so I wait here.
Your calendar is connected. Every meeting from it lands here by itself. Another account connects from the Settings tab.
Auto-record. Your meetings are here now. Auto-record picks which ones the recorder joins by itself: all, internal ones only, or the ones you select. The transcript is ready when the call ends.
Let the bot in. The recorder joins as a guest. When the host keeps a waiting room, someone has to let it in; otherwise nothing is recorded.
Or record one now. Paste any invite link from the Home page. Same recorder, no calendar needed.
Quick Find. Any recording in a moment. Ctrl K opens it from anywhere; Next opens it now.
Type what you remember. A word from the name of the recording. I typed one for you.
Every match. Each result is a recording. Click one to open it right there.
Every match. Each result is a recording. Tap one to open it right there.
Narrow it down. By folder, by type of recording, or by date.
Point at a paragraph. A small bar appears at its edge. I show it for you.
Press and hold a paragraph. A small bar appears at its edge. I show it for you.
Highlight, comment, copy. Highlight the paragraph in a colour, write a comment on it, or copy its text.
A colour is a label. Decision, question, to do: name the colours once and every highlight says what it is. Manage them from the same menu.
Or select a few words. Select the words you need: a bar above them highlights or comments on just those.
Everything in one place. Comments open a thread on the right. Highlights are listed there too, so a long call reads in a minute.
Trash. A deleted recording waits here. Nothing is gone at once.
Restore or delete for good. Open a row's menu: put it back where it was, or remove it forever.
This is Home. Four ways to make a transcript at the top, your recordings below, your plan and First steps on the right.
What Free includes. The files you have used this month and the day the count resets.
What Free includes. This button opens your plan: what Free includes and what an upgrade adds.
When you need more. Start the trial or upgrade, right from this card.
When you need more. Start the trial or upgrade from the same button.
Audio and video files. This card takes any recording from your computer. Next opens it.
Audio and video files. The plus button takes any recording from your phone. Next opens it.
Drop a file here. Or click to choose one, then press Start transcription. The step is done the moment the upload starts.
Drop a file here. Or tap to choose one, then press Start transcription. The step is done the moment the upload starts.
Instant speech. Talk, and the words appear as you speak. Next opens it.
Say a few words. Press Start recording and talk for a few seconds. Press the red Stop and the step is done.
Meeting Recorder. A bot joins a Zoom, Meet or Teams call and writes the notes. Next opens it.
Paste the invite link. Copy it from the calendar invite, paste it here and press Transcribe now. The step is done when the recorder is on its way.
Transcribe from URL. YouTube, Google Drive, Dropbox and more. Next opens it.
Paste a link. Any public video or audio link, then press Start transcription. The step is done the moment it starts.
Meetings. Your calendar lives here. Next takes you there.
Connect Google Calendar. Press Connect and sign in. Your meetings then show up here by themselves.
A calendar is already connected. This step is done. Another account connects from the Settings tab.
Open the welcome recording. I made this one for you, so you can try it on real text. Next opens it.
Press Apply template. Pick a shape: meeting notes, interview, action items. The summary is rewritten in it.
Fix a word. At 2:16 the model wrote "lunch" for "launch". Press Edit transcript, fix the word and press Save.
Fix a word. At 2:16 the model wrote "lunch" for "launch". Open More, press Edit transcript, fix the word and press Save.
My Records. Folders live on this page. Next takes you there.
Add Folder. This button makes a new folder. Next opens it.
Name it, press Create Folder. One folder per client or project. It shows up in your folders at once.
Three voices. Priya only said her first name on the call. Next opens the list so you can give her the full one.
Priya Nair, in full. Point at Priya and press the pencil. Type Priya Nair, press Enter.
Priya Nair, in full. Press the pencil next to Priya. Type Priya Nair, press Enter.
Priority processing is on. You know your way around now. From here your files are processed first, even at peak times, with our best model.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Thanks for joining, Priya. I'm Sam, I look after new accounts at Transcribe To Text, and Jordan here runs customer success. You said your week is full of calls and the notes never get written, so let's walk through what the app does with a call like this one.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: Great. I'm an independent researcher. I interview people for three clients, about eight calls a week, and every client wants the notes by Friday. Half the time I'm typing them from memory. Where would a recording even go?

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: Four ways in, all on the Home page. Drop an audio or video file, paste a link to a recording, press Record and speak into the microphone, or paste a Zoom, Meet or Teams link and our recorder joins the call for you.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: So the recorder is a bot that sits in the meeting?

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Yes. Connect your Google or Outlook calendar once and it joins the calls you choose by itself. Auto-record can take every meeting or only the ones you organise. The host lets it in like any guest, and the transcript writes itself while you talk.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: And when the file is in, what do I get back?

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: A transcript with every word, split by speaker, with the time next to each paragraph. Click any word and the audio plays from there. Speaker identification is automatic: leave it on Auto-detect, and set a number only if you know exactly how many people were on the call.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: The voices come out as Speaker 1 and Speaker 2 until you name them. That takes a few seconds, and from then on every quote says who said it. A client reading the notes sees that Priya asked this and the participant answered that, not Speaker 2.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: And when I need to hear a tricky bit again?

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: Click the word and it plays from there. The arrows step five seconds back or forward, and the speed runs from half to double. For clean reading, switch off the names and the timecodes, one switch each.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: Good. Some of my interviews happen over a phone line, and people mumble. How accurate is it?

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: Good enough that fixing is the exception. When the model does slip, Edit transcript lets you change the word right in the text, and the summary follows.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Quick aside: the launch of our noise-robust model is on the fourteenth, and every account gets it free for the first two weeks. Phone lines and busy cafes are exactly what it was trained on.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: Nice. Now the part my clients actually read. The summary?

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Every recording gets a summary on its own tab: key points, decisions, action items. Pick a template once, Meeting notes, Interview or Sales call, and every summary comes out in that shape. You can write your own template and apply it to any recording later.

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: The outline on the right lists the topics with their times, so you jump straight to the part about pricing. And for a long interview, mark what matters while you read: highlight a quote, leave a comment on it, tag a colleague. Everything you mark lands in the panel on the right, so an hour reads in a minute.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: One of my clients is in Mexico City. Can they read it in Spanish?

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Translate to Spanish, or any of the other languages, and the transcript and the summary appear on a second tab next to the original. Copy either one with one click.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: What about getting it out of the app? My clients want a Word document.

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: Export as PDF, Word, plain text or subtitles. The summary, the translation and the audio are switches: turn on what you need. One file or a whole folder at once. Sharing works the same way: invite people by email or turn on a link, and they see the recording, the transcript and the summary under Shared with me.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: Folders. Every client should have one.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: A folder per client, per study, whatever fits. Drag a recording in, star the important ones, and My Records keeps the whole archive. Quick Find searches what was said across every recording, so the one quote about pricing is found in the exact sentence of the exact interview. And a recording deleted by mistake waits in Trash until you empty it.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: Alright. On a normal week, what do I do differently?

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: Nothing. The calendar is connected, the recorder joins the calls, and the transcript and the summary wait in the folder. After each call a recap email can go out by itself, to everyone invited or only to you. On Friday you open the client's folder, export the summaries and send them.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: What does it cost me?

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Free covers your first recordings, so you can try everything. Pro removes the limits and adds long files, priority processing and the team features for when you bring someone in. The plan page says exactly what is in each.

welcome.speaker: Priya
welcome.text: Sounds like a plan. I'll try it for two weeks on the next study, and we check in on Friday.

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: Done. I'll set up a folder for that study today and connect your calendar on tomorrow's call.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: And this recording is your first one. Open the summary, name the speakers, fix the word I misread, and the first three steps are done. Thanks, Priya.
